decode_smoke.output_verbatim: A circuit breaker is a safety feature in electrical circuits that helps prevent overloads and prevents damage to the system. It works by temporarily shutting off power to a section of the circuit when it detects a fault, such as a short circuit or a damaged component. This prevents the circuit from overheating and potentially causing a fire or other hazards. Circuit breakers are typically installed in high-voltage circuits, such as those used in power grids, and are designed to protect the system from damage caused by excessive current flow.
